compatibility_rule: Components exchange `hello` frames listing supported protocol versions as MAJOR.MINOR strings. A peer accepts a message only if its MAJOR equals a supported MAJOR and its MINOR is less than or equal to the highest supported MINOR for that MAJOR. Unknown fields are rejected, not ignored. Incompatible peers receive error code PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE with both version lists so the UI can tell the customer which component to update.

rules.terminal_result: Every command the controller sends is terminated by exactly one `result` frame per command_id (origin `agent` or `relay`). `error` frames are only used when no command_id is known (malformed frame, protocol error, subscription errors). Relay-side rejections before forwarding (signature, ownership, grant, rate limit, PC offline, queue full) are `result{origin:'relay', state:'failed', error}` and mean the PC never received the command. Once the relay has written a command to the agent's socket, nothing the relay observes can prove the command did not run: an agent connection lost after forwarding yields `result{origin:'relay', state:'outcome_unknown', error:OUTCOME_UNKNOWN}` whether or not an ack was seen; the agent's own journaled result may correct it once (see late_results). Clients therefore never present a relay `outcome_unknown` as 'nothing ran'.
rules.duplicate_command: An identical re-submission (same command_id, same signed payload bytes) is answered by re-emitting the previous `result` (or the current ack while still running). The same command_id with different payload bytes is rejected with COMMAND_ID_REUSED.
rules.command_window_and_confirmation: The command's issued_at/expires_at window is checked once when the PC receives the command. Once the PC has emitted confirmation_required, the challenge's expires_at governs: the signed confirmation is accepted iff the challenge is unexpired and unconsumed, and the command then proceeds regardless of its own expires_at. Controllers default disruptive commands to default_confirmed_command_lifetime_seconds so the two windows do not cross by accident.
rules.grants_snapshot: The PC's locally approved controller store (written only at local pairing approval) is the sole source of controller public keys. grants_snapshot is a revocation/intersection list: a kid is usable only if it is locally approved AND present in the latest snapshot; effective capabilities = local ∩ snapshot. A snapshot can never add a controller or widen a grant.
rules.challenge_text: A confirmation challenge travels as an opaque string (challenge_text). The PC stores the exact string it emitted; the relay validates it by strict-parsing a copy and forwards the original string verbatim; the controller strict-parses it once for display and hashes the string verbatim into challenge_digest.
rules.pairing_secret: The PC generates the pairing code locally. The backend only ever receives SHA-256 of the code as a lookup handle; the phone transfers the code out of band (QR or typing) and both devices derive the 6-digit verification code with HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the code, so a backend that substitutes a controller key cannot make the two displays agree. Since 1.4 the PC also pins its own identity key for the phone: on approve the agent sends pairing_decision.pc_key_mac = base64url(HMAC-SHA256(key = the normalised code, msg = "dome-pair-pc-key-v1|" + pairing_id + "|" + pc_id + "|" + controller_kid + "|" + pc_kid)), all 32 bytes, so a backend that substitutes the PC's public key cannot make the MAC verify either (rules.pc_key_pinning).
rules.controller_socket_identity: A controller hello MUST carry kid and, to be bound, proof: an ES256 envelope signed by that key over a hello_proof payload {type, protocol_version, kid, account_id, issued_at, expires_at, nonce} (relay-frames#/$defs/hello_proof). The relay verifies the signature with the JWK of the controller row (session account, kid), checks envelope.kid == payload.kid == hello.kid, payload.account_id == the session's account, the time window (lifetime <= confirmation_challenge_lifetime_seconds, skew max_clock_skew_seconds) and that the nonce has not been seen before; only then does it bind the socket to the controller row and report hello_ack.controller_id. A hello without proof, or whose kid has no non-revoked controller row in the account, stays unbound (hello_ack without controller_id; such a socket may only poll pairing status via REST). A proof that is present but fails any check is answered with error UNKNOWN_KEY and close 4003. subscribe/command/confirmation/cancel require a bound, non-revoked controller; every envelope's kid must equal the socket's kid (else UNKNOWN_KEY and close 4003). Revocation sends `revoked` to all sockets bound to that controller and closes them. Controllers announce protocol_versions including 1.1 to use input_batch frames and including 1.4 to use the screen_* frames; older peers never receive them.
rules.state_cache: The relay keeps the last `state` frame per online PC and re-sends it (unchanged) after pc_status on every accepted subscribe. The agent sends a `state` frame immediately after applying grants_snapshot and then on change (debounced 500 ms) and every 30 s.
rules.in_flight: In-flight commands per PC = rows in created|accepted|executing|awaiting_confirmation. The relay gives each forwarded command a hard deadline = max(expires_at, received_at + timeout_ms) + (confirmation_challenge_lifetime_seconds if confirmation==challenge) + 10 s; at the deadline it emits result{origin:relay, state:outcome_unknown, error:OUTCOME_UNKNOWN} (the command was forwarded, so the relay cannot know whether it ran) and frees the slot. Armed power countdowns are exempt until fires_at + timeout_ms.
rules.late_results: After the relay closed a command as outcome_unknown, the agent's journaled result MAY be forwarded once as a correction result{origin:agent}; the controller treats it as replacing the prior outcome. A successful socket write is not delivery: on every reconnect the agent re-sends every terminal result that was never written to a socket and every terminal result finished after the last frame it received on the previous connection. Any other post-terminal result is dropped and logged.
rules.mismatch_handling: A command whose account_id/target_pc_id do not match the agent's stored identity is answered result{origin:agent, failed, ACCOUNT_MISMATCH|TARGET_PC_MISMATCH}, is NOT journaled, is logged as a local security event; three within 60 s make the agent close the socket and reconnect with backoff.
rules.agent_identity: The agent's pc_id/account_id are fixed at link time. If hello_ack.pc_id or grants_snapshot.pc_id/account_id differ, the agent closes the socket, stops reconnecting and shows a local re-link prompt. A command received before the connection's first grants_snapshot is answered result{failed, PC_RECONNECTING} and not journaled.
rules.plan_state: pc_enabled=false or controller status=plan_disabled in grants_snapshot are plan/account states, never revocations: local grants stay, the relay refuses routing (PC_PLAN_DISABLED / CONTROLLER_PLAN_DISABLED) and the agent refuses independently.
rules.token_and_entitlement_refresh: PC access tokens are validated only at WebSocket upgrade; an open socket is never closed for token expiry; the agent fetches a new token before reconnecting whenever less than 5 minutes remain. Entitlement assertions follow schemas/entitlement.schema.json: refreshed on connect and at 80% of lifetime; grace only on network error/5xx.
rules.pairing_offline: A claim against an offline PC is accepted (202, state claimed); the relay delivers pairing_request on the agent's next connect (after grants_snapshot) for every unexpired claimed session; the phone polls GET /v1/pairing/{pairing_id}. Pairing session, request and code share one expires_at.
rules.coalescing: Coalescing group = (coalesce key, canonical target JSON or '' when null) per PC across all controllers. The superseded command terminates as result{state:canceled, error:COMMAND_SUPERSEDED, result omitted} and is journaled as such.
rules.input_sessions: Manual touchpad/keyboard input (actions.json capabilities `pointer` and `keyboard`, both Free) is human-directed and travels in a bounded signed stream, not in commands. (1) Session: the controller sends the registry action input.session_start (permitted when its grant holds pointer or keyboard; params.takeover replaces another controller's session). The agent issues a fresh 22-character input_session_id and a lease of input_lease_seconds and answers input_session_result{input_session_id, lease_seconds, input_age_budget_ms, max_batch_events, pointer, keyboard, foreground_app?}. Exactly one controller owns a PC's session at a time; a second controller without takeover gets INPUT_SESSION_OWNED. Takeover, controller revocation, grant narrowing, pc switching, remote-control disable, Windows session lock, a secure desktop, lease expiry, agent restart or the relay losing the controller's socket END the session: the agent first retires the session id so delayed batches cannot press anything, then releases every button and key THAT SESSION injected (never the physical keyboard's), then sends input_session{event:ended, reason, holds_released}. (2) Batches: each controller_input_batch frame carries an envelope signed by the controller key over input_batch_payload{type:input_batch, protocol_version, account_id, controller_id, target_pc_id, input_session_id, seq, issued_at, expires_at, events[<= input_batch_max_events]} with expires_at - issued_at <= input_batch_lifetime_seconds. The relay verifies the signature with the socket's key record, binds account/controller, requires a live grant whose capabilities cover every event type (pointer_* need pointer, pointer_move_to and pointer_wheel included; text/key/shortcut need keyboard; INPUT_NOT_PERMITTED), requires the PC online and past its first snapshot (PC_OFFLINE / PC_RECONNECTING), applies plans.json input_rate_limit per controller (RATE_LIMITED), forwards the envelope verbatim and keeps NO commands row and NO security event per accepted batch. The agent re-verifies the signature against its local grant, requires input_session_id to be the live session owned by this controller (INPUT_SESSION_REQUIRED / INPUT_SESSION_EXPIRED), requires seq strictly greater than the last accepted seq (INPUT_SEQUENCE_INVALID: the batch is dropped, the session continues), requires the batch's age <= input_age_budget_ms, where age is measured against the controller's clock offset estimated per session (the minimum of receipt time minus issued_at over a recent window, seeded at input.session_start) so that phone/PC clock skew neither blocks input nor defeats the check; the relay's received_at stamp bounds the relay-to-agent leg the same way (INPUT_STALE: the batch is dropped) and renews the lease on every valid batch (an empty events array is a pure keepalive). Rejections are counted in input_ack.dropped_events and reported to the batch's controller as error{error, ref_pc_id, ref_input_session_id}: the agent sends error{error, ref_input_session_id, ref_controller_id} (at most one per code per second), the relay checks that ref_controller_id belongs to the PC's account, strips it, adds ref_pc_id and delivers the frame only to that controller's protocol-1.1 sockets. Input rejections never terminate a command. (2a) Screen view events (1.4): pointer_move_to{x, y, gen} is an absolute position normalised to 0..65535 over the surface of the PC's live screen session, never PC pixels; the agent accepts it only while a screen session owned by the batch's controller is live (SCREEN_SESSION_REQUIRED) and only when gen equals the current geometry generation (SCREEN_GEOMETRY_CHANGED); a failing batch is dropped and counted in input_ack.dropped_events with at most one error frame per code per second, which the relay routes to the issuing controller exactly like INPUT_* rejections, and the input session continues. pointer_wheel{dx, dy} is wheel motion in Windows wheel units (120 = one notch, |dx|,|dy| <= input_wheel_max). Within a batch, consecutive pointer_move_to events may be coalesced to the last one (last position wins); they are never summed and never merged with relative pointer_move. (3) Dispatch: adjacent pointer_move events within a batch may be summed; nothing is ever merged across a button, scroll, text, key or shortcut event, and ordering is preserved. If dispatch falls behind by more than input_age_budget_ms the agent discards pending events, suspends the session (input_session{event:suspended, reason:backpressure}) and requires a fresh input.session_start. Old traffic is never replayed after a reconnect or restart; the journal is not used for input. (4) Acks: the agent sends input_ack{input_session_id, last_seq, accepted_events, dropped_events, held_buttons, held_keys} at most four times per second while a session is live; it reports Windows acceptance, never an observed application effect. (5) Content: text events are literal customer input; no component logs, journals, persists, or forwards them to an AI provider, and the relay sees them only in transit (TLS, not end-to-end). AI and routines cannot use pointer, keyboard, text, key or shortcut primitives (rules.ai_eligibility).
rules.grant_update: The PC's local approval is the only source of a controller's capabilities. When the owner changes a grant locally (for example grants pointer and keyboard to an already-paired phone, or removes them), the agent sends grant_update{controller_id, kid, capabilities}; the relay replaces the grant row's capabilities with exactly that list (it may widen or narrow), re-pushes grants_snapshot and the account's device list reflects it. Existing grants never gain pointer, keyboard, screen or screen_audio implicitly: the capabilities are absent until the PC owner adds them in a DoMe window on the PC (rules.local_permission_ui); screen_audio is accepted only together with screen (INVALID_PARAMETERS on the grant change). Narrowing a grant that removes screen ends that controller's live screen session (grant_removed). grants_snapshot remains an intersection list and cannot add capabilities the PC did not store.
rules.ai_eligibility: Actions with ai_eligible:false (every input.* and screen.* action), the input_batch primitives, the screen and screen_audio media, the screen signaling frames (screen_ice_request, screen_ice_servers, screen_answer, screen_session, screen_usage, screen_allowance) and the screen data channel never enter an AI provider's tool catalogue, a saved routine or a layout shortcut. Typing literal text through the keyboard capability is UI input to whatever the PC has focused; it is not parsed by the deterministic text-command parser or any model and never invokes shell execution inside the agent.
rules.command_version_stamping: A controller stamps each signed payload with the lowest protocol version that defines it: a command carries its action's `since` (actions.json; absent = 1.0); a confirmation carries the protocol_version of the command it confirms; an input_batch carries the lowest version that defines every event in it: 1.1 for the 1.1 events, 1.4 when it contains pointer_move_to, pointer_wheel or key f11 (the shared libraries' input_batch_protocol_version). Verifiers (relay and agent) also refuse a command whose protocol_version is below its action's `since`, and an input_batch below the version its events need, with PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE (detail {peer, required}). So a phone update never breaks older PCs: an agent that predates an action answers PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE for that action only (its MINOR is too high for the agent) and keeps executing every older action. Check order (1.4): verifiers check protocol compatibility and `since` BEFORE schema validation, so a payload from a newer MINOR with fields or events this peer does not know yields PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE, never MALFORMED_MESSAGE; a protocol_version that is not a MAJOR.MINOR string falls through to schema validation (MALFORMED_MESSAGE). Agents shipped before 1.4 validate the schema first and would answer a 1.4-stamped batch with MALFORMED_MESSAGE, so the relay refuses an input_batch whose stamp is not compatible with the target agent's announced protocol_versions before forwarding it (error PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE detail {peer: "agent", required}) and refuses screen.* commands to an agent that did not announce 1.4 the same way. A hello_proof carries the controller's own protocol_version (only the relay checks it, and the relay is deployed before the PCs).
rules.bridge_negotiation: bridge_hello lists every MINOR the extension speaks. bridge_hello_ack.protocol_version is the negotiated version: the highest MINOR both sides support within their highest common MAJOR (under the compatibility rule a side that supports a MINOR also accepts every lower one); the extension accepts the ack only if it is compatible with its own list. The agent sends a bridge op added in a later MINOR (bridge.schema.json; search and open_result since 1.2) only to an extension whose negotiated version includes it, and otherwise fails the command with EXTENSION_UPDATE_REQUIRED without sending anything.
rules.window_actions: app.maximize, app.restore and app.set_fullscreen act only on visible, un-owned, uncloaked top-level windows of processes whose executable path equals the approved entry. They never start the app (APP_NOT_RUNNING). app.set_fullscreen presses exactly one F11 into the approved window, and only after Windows reports that window foreground immediately before the press and no modifier key is held (FOCUS_DENIED / ACTION_UNAVAILABLE, nothing pressed); it is not keyboard input in the sense of rules.input_sessions and needs only `apps`. An app that does not enter full screen is FULLSCREEN_UNSUPPORTED and is never maximised instead. A window of a process running as administrator is APP_ELEVATED. On failure the result carries the best-known app_window_state_result.
rules.search_queries: youtube.search query text is customer-typed content. No component logs, journals, persists or forwards it except inside the signed command (the relay keeps only the command digest) and the bridge_request that carries it to the extension, and, only for an account with current assistant consent, inside the body of POST /v1/assistant/turn (the owner's words, which may contain search text, and the AI-proposed youtube.search step in its response) and cloud-api's request to the AI provider, which cloud-api never logs or stores. The phone never puts search text from a command it handled without AI into an assistant request. Validation errors never echo it. The extension places it only in the search_query parameter of https://www.youtube.com/results via URLSearchParams. Results and the results-page tab never echo it (the results tab carries no title).
rules.ai_allowance: One AI request is one charged assistant turn. The 5-hour window and the weekly window (plans.json ai_window / ai_week) each start at the account's first request while none is open and end after their length; a request needs room in both, otherwise the top-up balance (ai_topup_allowed plans only), otherwise it is refused with AI_ALLOWANCE_EXHAUSTED{reason, resets_at}. Free's ai_taste_requests never renews. Everyday commands the phone resolves itself never count. The entitlement assertion's plan claim is 'pro' for every paid plan.
rules.screen_sessions: Screen view (actions.json capabilities `screen` and `screen_audio`, both granted only on the PC) streams the PC's picture to one phone over WebRTC between the two devices; the relay carries signaling only (rules.screen_signaling) and never media. (1) One session per PC. screen.session_start{offer_sdp, surface, audio, takeover} from a controller whose grant holds screen makes the agent issue a fresh 22-character screen_session_id and answer screen_session_result{screen_session_id, surfaces, surface_index, gen, audio, lease_seconds, allowance, consent, encoder?}; a second controller gets SCREEN_SESSION_OWNED unless it sends takeover: true, and the old session ends `takeover`; a restart by the same controller ends its own session `replaced`. The PC captures nothing until DTLS has connected to the certificate whose fingerprint is in the offer it verified, and it refuses to start unless remote control is on, the Windows session is unlocked and not on the secure desktop, relay.screen is present and valid, the consent rules below are satisfied and the offer passes the strict SDP check (SCREEN_OFFER_INVALID). (2) Indicator, fail-closed: before the worker starts the agent creates a 'Screen view on' bar on every monitor and the tray badge and confirms each window exists; if it cannot, the start is SCREEN_CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE{detail: indicator} and nothing is captured; while a bar is missing (monitor change) capture pauses (`indicator`), and after 10 s the session ends capture_failed. No setting hides the indicator and no phone or server can. (3) Viewer lease: the phone sends `hb` on the data channel every screen_heartbeat_seconds; no heartbeat for screen_lease_seconds ends the session viewer_gone. (4) Allowance tickets (dead-man switch): the agent sends screen_usage{screen_session_id, live_seconds, relayed, relayed_bytes} about screen_allowance_renew_before_seconds before relay.screen.granted_until and the relay answers screen_allowance{screen_session_id, granted_until, unlimited, final, reason?, resets_at?} in screen_allowance_chunk_seconds chunks; when granted_until passes without a new ticket the agent ends the session: allowance_exhausted when the relay said final with no other reason, controller_offline when reason is controller_offline, otherwise allowance_unconfirmed. A PC cut off from the relay therefore stops within one chunk on every plan; the relay socket's loss alone does not end a session, and after the agent reconnects grants_snapshot is applied first (a revocation ends the session) before tickets resume. The relay answers final with reason controller_offline when the owning controller has had no bound socket for 60 s or its sockets were closed by revocation, logout or account-session revocation, and sends that frame at once if a ticket is outstanding, so signing a phone out ends its Screen view within one chunk. (5) Consent: ask mode (a per-grant local setting) and the PC-wide post-Stop cooldown (set when someone at the PC presses Stop; length = the longest setting among the PC's screen grants, default screen_pc_stop_cooldown_default_seconds; it applies to EVERY controller) show a consent window at the PC; Deny is SCREEN_CONSENT_DECLINED, no answer within screen_consent_timeout_seconds is SCREEN_CONSENT_TIMEOUT. At most one consent window opens per minute per PC, and after a Deny or a timeout further starts from every controller are refused with SCREEN_CONSENT_DECLINED and no window for 1, 2, 5, then 10 minutes per consecutive refusal (reset by an Allow or by the cooldown ending); the window also offers a 1-hour per-controller block (SCREEN_CONSENT_DECLINED, no window) and 'turn off Screen view for this phone' (grant_update without screen and screen_audio). A takeover never skips a consent window the stopped phone would have faced. (6) Ending, in this order: retire the id (late data-channel messages and pointer_move_to are dropped) -> tell the worker to stop, wait at most 2 s, then terminate it -> close the bars only once the worker has exited -> screen_session{event: ended, reason, live_seconds} -> local notification and history row (phone, times, reason, seconds; no content) -> revoke the phone's TURN credential (relay, best effort). Reasons: stopped (phone: `bye` on the data channel or screen.session_stop, whichever first), stopped_on_pc (bar, tray, hotkey; starts the cooldown; the phone never restarts by itself), replaced, viewer_gone, takeover, controller_revoked, controller_offline, grant_removed, plan_disabled, remote_disabled (ends before the disable returns and refuses new starts), session_locked (lock ends at once), secure_desktop (a UAC or other secure desktop PAUSES capture with screen_session{paused, secure_desktop} and the data-channel state message; resumed when it closes; after screen_secure_desktop_pause_max_seconds paused the session ends), allowance_exhausted, allowance_unconfirmed, max_duration (screen_session_max_seconds; a longer view needs a fresh signed start), capture_failed (worker crash or rebuild failure), connection_failed (no DTLS within screen_connect_timeout_seconds), agent_restart (recorded on the next start). Every stop works offline; no server is involved. (7) Frames: the agent sends screen_session{started, path: direct|relayed} after DTLS connected and the first frame was sent, paused/resumed with the cause, and ended with the reason and live_seconds; the relay forwards them to the owner and broadcasts them to the PC's subscribers that announced 1.4 (older sockets never receive them). No pc_state field changes in 1.4; other phones learn of ownership from SCREEN_SESSION_OWNED and these frames. Results and frames carry ids, geometry, flags, reasons and seconds only: no SDP, no title, no address.
rules.screen_signaling: Signaling is authenticated end to end with the keys DoMe already has, and the relay routes it without being able to alter it. (1) ICE servers: the phone sends screen_ice_request{pc_id} on a bound controller socket that announced 1.4. The relay checks a live grant with screen for this controller on this PC, the PC online and past its first snapshot, the allowance not exhausted, the rate limits (plans.json screen_ice_rate_limit), the per-account TURN caps and the operator switch (SCREEN_VIEW_DISABLED), mints a TURN credential for the PHONE only, bound to this controller with at most one outstanding credential per controller (minting a new one first revokes the previous), and answers screen_ice_servers{pc_id, ice_servers, expires_at, allowance, turn: available|unavailable|disabled}. The credential is revoked when no screen.session_start from that controller arrives within screen_start_command_lifetime_seconds, on every start refusal, at the end of the session, when the sweeper ends a session, and on controller revocation, grant narrowing that removes screen, logout, account-session revocation or plan change. The PC never receives a TURN credential: relay.screen.stun_urls only. (2) The offer: the phone builds a receive-only RTCPeerConnection (video and audio transceivers recvonly, one data channel named dome-screen-v1), gathers all candidates (vanilla ICE: no candidate ever travels separately) and signs screen.session_start{offer_sdp, surface, audio, takeover} with its controller key, so its DTLS fingerprint is inside the signed bytes. The controller gives the command a lifetime of screen_start_command_lifetime_seconds (the consent wait must fit; max_command_lifetime_seconds still bounds it) and the command window is checked once at receipt. (3) The relay applies the route_command checks, requires that the agent socket announced 1.4 (else result{origin: relay, failed, PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE detail{peer: agent, required: 1.4}}), reserves the first allowance chunk (else result{origin: relay, failed, SCREEN_ALLOWANCE_EXHAUSTED detail{resets_at}}) and forwards the envelope verbatim with relay.screen{granted_until|null, unlimited, stun_urls, relayed_max_kbps?}; the commands row stores only the digest. (4) The agent re-verifies the command against its LOCAL grant, applies the strict SDP check (at most screen_sdp_max_bytes; printable ASCII plus CRLF only; exactly one a=fingerprint:sha-256 value; m-lines exactly video recvonly, audio recvonly and one application section; H.264 or VP8 offered; anything else is SCREEN_OFFER_INVALID), and only then spawns the worker, which produces a send-only answer with a fresh per-session DTLS certificate. (5) The answer: the agent signs screen_answer_payload{type: screen_answer, protocol_version: 1.4, account_id, pc_id, controller_id, command_id, screen_session_id, offer_digest = base64url SHA-256 of the exact offer_sdp bytes, answer_sdp, issued_at, expires_at} (lifetime at most screen_answer_lifetime_seconds) with the PC's identity key (envelope kid = pc_kid) and sends screen_answer{envelope, ref_controller_id}. The relay checks that the controller belongs to the PC's account and holds a live screen grant, strips the reference and delivers screen_answer{pc_id, envelope} only to that controller's sockets that announced 1.4, preferring the socket that issued the command; never to subscribers (SDP contains addresses); no commands row, no log content. The answer is never carried in a result, because results are journaled on the PC and SDP must never be persisted; the phone waits for the result and the answer in either order. (6) The phone accepts the answer only if all hold: envelope.kid equals the pc_kid pinned at pairing for that pc_id (rules.pc_key_pinning); the signature verifies with the pinned JWK; account_id, controller_id, pc_id and command_id are its own; offer_digest matches the offer it sent; the window is fresh within max_clock_skew_seconds; every a=fingerprint:sha-256 in answer_sdp is identical. Then it applies exactly the signed answer_sdp string. Anything else is SCREEN_ANSWER_INVALID and shows nothing; there is no 'continue anyway'. (7) Capture starts only after the DTLS handshake succeeds against the fingerprint in the phone-signed offer (aiortc fails the handshake on a mismatch), so a relay that rewrites either SDP breaks a signature and one that forwards both unchanged sees fingerprints and ICE passwords, which are not enough to join the DTLS session. The data channel is authenticated by the same DTLS session, so heartbeats and bye need no per-message signature. (8) No renegotiation, ever: any transport change (network change, another monitor, recovery) is a new signed session; a replayed start is answered with the journaled result and starts nothing (rules.duplicate_command); a replayed answer fails the command_id and offer_digest checks.
rules.pc_key_pinning: The phone trusts a PC's screen answer only when it is signed by the identity key the PC pinned at pairing, so a malicious relay cannot substitute a PC key and show a fake screen. (1) On local approval the agent, which still holds the pairing code, computes pc_key_mac = base64url(HMAC-SHA256(key = normalised pairing code (ASCII), msg = "dome-pair-pc-key-v1|" + pairing_id + "|" + pc_id + "|" + controller_kid + "|" + pc_kid)), all 32 bytes untruncated (43 base64url characters), where pc_kid is kid_from_jwk of the PC's identity public key, and sends it in pairing_decision.pc_key_mac. (2) The relay stores the MAC on the pairing row and, once the state is approved and never before, GET /v1/pairing/{id} returns pairing_status_response.pc_key{public_jwk, mac} with the JWK from the server's PC row; approved rows stay readable for at least 5 minutes after approval so the phone's poll can fetch it. (3) The phone keeps the normalised code (or an HMAC key derived from it) only until the poll returns approved, computes pc_kid = kid_from_jwk(public_jwk), verifies the MAC in constant time with the code as the key, stores {pc_id, pc_kid, pc_public_jwk, pinned_at} next to its controller key and then discards the code; the code still never reaches the URL, storage or logs, and a pairing that ends declined, expired or abandoned discards it too. (4) The server knows only SHA-256 of the code (pairing_code_handle); the code is 20 Crockford symbols (100 bits), so a MAC for a substitute key cannot be ground out. (5) Failures are honest and final: no pin for a pc_id (the phone left before approval, or the agent is older than 1.4 and sent no pc_key_mac) means Screen view is refused on the phone with SCREEN_PC_UNVERIFIED ('pair again'); an answer whose kid differs from the pin, or whose signature fails under the pinned JWK, is SCREEN_ANSWER_INVALID and the session is abandoned; a PC re-linked with a new identity key must be paired again. There is no 'continue anyway' and the pin is never updated from a relay frame. Existing pairings re-pair once.
rules.screen_metering: Free Screen view minutes are a SERVER ledger settled on the relay's own clock; the phone cannot change them and the PC cannot buy minutes with what it reports. (1) Ledger: per account, a rolling window of plans.json screen_view_window_hours starting at the first use while none is open, with screen_view_seconds_per_window seconds (null = unlimited; those plans receive unlimited: true tickets, still in chunks, so the dead-man latency is the same). (2) Gate: the relay refuses screen_ice_request and screen.session_start when nothing is left (result{origin: relay, failed, SCREEN_ALLOWANCE_EXHAUSTED, detail{resets_at}}; the PC never sees the command) and reserves screen_allowance_chunk_seconds at the start and at each screen_usage renewal; when nothing is left it answers no new ticket (final: true). (3) Settlement on the relay's clock, never on the agent's figures: the charge for a session is the wall time the relay measured from the moment it forwarded screen.session_start (or from the first `started` frame it saw, as the operator configures; default forwarding) to the `ended` frame or, if none arrives, to the end of the last ticket, rounded up to 10 s and capped at the total reserved. live_seconds from screen_usage never reduces it (it serves dashboards only). connection_failed settles to 0 only when the relay saw NO `started` frame AND at most screen_connect_timeout_seconds passed since forwarding, and at most 3 such zero-charged attempts are accepted per window per account (the fourth is charged its measured seconds). Agent-reported pauses are honoured only as a bounded discount: at most screen_secure_desktop_pause_max_seconds per session and only for pauses the relay itself saw as a paused->resumed pair on its own clock; minutes may count while the PC shows a permission prompt. The unused part of the last chunk is refunded once per session, never more than the relay-measured remainder, and only for sessions the relay remembers (after a relay restart no refund). A sweeper charges an unreported reservation in full. Setup time counts. (4) TURN: credentials are minted for the phone only with TTL = remaining allowance + 60 s (Free, at most 3600) or screen_session_max_seconds (unlimited plans), bound to one controller and revoked on every end and refusal path (rules.screen_signaling); relayed bytes are reconciled from the TURN provider's own usage figures, never from screen_usage.relayed_bytes, and per-account daily and monthly caps refuse further minting (turn: disabled). (5) Rate limits: screen_ice_request per plans.json screen_ice_rate_limit (per controller, plus the per-account hourly figure); screen.session_start per screen_start_rate_limit (per controller). (6) The phone's remaining-time display comes from screen_ice_servers.allowance, screen_session_result.allowance and the data-channel allowance message, for display only; the PC's ended{allowance_exhausted} is authoritative. A patched agent can take unlimited minutes only on a direct path, which costs DoMe nothing; relayed use is bounded without trusting either device.
rules.screen_content: Nothing is recorded and the AI never sees the stream. No component writes a frame or an audio sample to disk, logs it, includes it in diagnostics, sends it to cloud-api or sends it to an AI provider; the picture and sound travel DTLS-SRTP between the PC's worker and the phone only, and the relay and the TURN provider see ciphertext, addresses and timing. No SDP, ICE candidate, IP address or TURN credential may appear in logs, journals, results, diagnostics bundles, security events or storage: the keys offer_sdp, answer_sdp, sdp, candidate, ice_servers, credential and username are redacted everywhere, the agent and worker pin the aioice and aiortc loggers to WARNING regardless of the configured level, free-text redaction masks IPv4 and IPv6 addresses with an optional :port (loopback included), the worker's stderr passes through the same redacting pipeline, and the screen answer travels in a frame, never in a journaled result. screen_session_result, screen_session frames and the local history carry ids, geometry, flags, reasons and seconds only. The screen data channel (screen_dc_message) is a closed vocabulary: hb, keyframe, bye and audio{on} from the phone; geometry, state, allowance and restricted from the PC; messages are at most screen_dc_message_max_bytes, unknown or malformed messages are dropped, and no data-channel message can inject input, change a grant or run anything on the PC (input stays on the signed input_batch path). screen.session_start and screen.session_stop are ai_eligible: false and routine_allowed: false (rules.ai_eligibility).
rules.local_permission_ui: The capabilities screen, screen_audio, pointer and keyboard are granted only in a DoMe window on the PC where the owner reads the scope text and confirms: never by the phone, never by the server (grants_snapshot intersects; pairing_decision.granted_capabilities never carries them at pairing) and never by a bare command-line flag (the CLI opens the same window and waits; headless widening works only on the fake platform, for tests). screen_audio is accepted only together with screen. Turning ask mode off or shortening the post-Stop cooldown counts as widening and needs the window too; narrowing is immediate everywhere. DoMe never injects phone input into its own permission UI: while a DoMe permission window is open (pairing approval, grant window, consent window, a Stop-menu confirmation) the input dispatcher drops every pointer_button and keyboard event from every phone, counts them in input_ack.dropped_events and reports INPUT_PAUSED_ON_PC at most once per second; before injecting a button press the agent compares the cursor position with the rectangles of its own bars and windows and drops a press that would land on them (INPUT_TARGET_RESERVED); the indicator bar never takes keyboard focus. A phone therefore cannot click its own Allow, and an accidental tap cannot press Stop or start the cooldown.
